Initially freeze the pretrained vision encoder and language model and train the projection/adapter on image–text pairs. This aligns visual features with the language model's input space while limiting early destructive updates. Next, unfreeze selected layers or adapters for instruction tuning, using lower learning rates for pretrained weights and diverse text/vision evaluation. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08485) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12597)

This staged recipe is a useful baseline, not a universal necessity. Data scale, domain shift, and architecture may justify joint training or continued freezing. Check whether the model actually uses the image through counterfactual image swaps and visual grounding tests. Monitor language-only performance, OCR, spatial reasoning, and hallucinations. A low alignment loss can hide shortcut learning from captions or answer priors rather than visual understanding.
